options.content: **operated_by attribution** — proving every bead write is traceable to a real human operator rather than a sentinel. Read it as a chain: the header must *arrive* (M1), the write must be classified **real** rather than sentinel/empty (M2, M8), the resolver must not *error* or fall back (M3, M4), and ambiguous agent names (M5) must stay at zero. The authoring gate (M9) is the enforcement point for human-authored bead types.

panels.title: Feature flag
panels.description: BEADS_OPERATED_BY_ENABLED — derived from the `kind=real` writes/total-writes ratio. 'OFF' when no real writes are landing (matches a pre-flag deploy); 'ON' when the resolver is producing oidc:/slack: values.

panels.title: M1: header arrival rate by auth_type & header_present
panels.description: Rate of inbound requests carrying X-Operated-By, by auth_type. Pre-flip the operator reads {auth_type="static",header_present="true"} as the precondition for flipping the flag (R9 §3.2 step 1). M1 increments BEFORE the feature flag is consulted.

panels.title: M2: write classification by kind & provider
panels.description: Audit-row writes classified by operated_by kind and provider. The 'real / total' ratio is the soak threshold (R9 §3.3). Pre-flip the ratio is 0 by design; post-flip it should rise to ~1 minus the agent-bead-fallback miss rate.

links.title: Drill into a single provider / kind (this board, filtered)
links.tooltip: Open this same board scoped to one provider and kind via the $provider/$kind vars — the per-provider detail the flat classification view lacks.

panels.title: Real writes ratio
panels.description: Share of audit writes resolving to a real operator (slack:|oidc:). Soak threshold: ≥ 0.95 in prod for 24h before flipping the flag globally (R9 §3.3).

panels.title: M3: resolver errors by error_type
panels.description: Resolver error counts. error_type ∈ {sanitize_reject, agent_lookup_fail, unexpected}. Sustained nonzero rate is a direct rollback signal (R9 §4.3 OperatedByResolverErrors). 'unexpected' must always be 0 — it is the 'something is very wrong' bucket. gardenio_beads_operated_by_resolver_errors_total is an only-on-error counter (kbeads/internal/server/operated_by_metrics.go) — it creates a series ONLY when a resolver error occurs, so the query is baselined with `or vector(0)` to plot an honest flat 0 (= 'no resolver errors — healthy') rather than a bare 'No data' that reads like a broken/unwired panel. A visible non-zero line is a direct rollback signal.

defaults.noValue: resolver not reporting — no gardenio_beads_operated_by_writes_total samples in window, so the error rate is UNKNOWN (not 0)

panels.title: M4: agent-bead fallback outcome
panels.description: Outcome of the static-token agent-bead inheritance fallback (R9 §4.1). result=resolved means the agent's bead carried a usable slack_user_id; result=empty means the CLI plumbing is broken or the agent's bead is missing the field.

panels.title: M5: ambiguous agent name detections
panels.description: Agent name re-used across spawns (R7 §6.6). Must be 0. Pages immediately when nonzero via OperatedByAmbiguousAgent (R9 §4.3) — the increment site is the offline backfill tool.

panels.title: Reference-extraction throughput by source field
panels.description: sum by (source_field)(rate(gardenio_beads_references_extracted_total[1h])) — the typed-mention / dep-graph extractor, broken down by which part of the bead the reference was found in (title / description / notes / comment). Every kbeads write (CreateBead / UpdateBead / AddComment) runs a regex pass that extracts ka-0000001713 references and persists them into bead_references; this counter bumps per source_field. A live pipeline (1200+ refs extracted) that had zero dashboard presence before this panel. description dominates, with comment/title/notes trailing.

panels.title: Operator-activity leaderboard by surface (24h)
panels.description: topk(10, sum by (surface)(increase(gardenio_operator_activity_total[24h]))) — which surface operators are mutating through: kbeads (CLI), slack (gb / bridge), or web (beads-viewer). gardenio_operator_activity_total is the operator-attributed engagement counter shared by the bridge (surface=slack) and beads-viewer (surface=web); kbeads owns the CLI-mutation slice. 1300+ activity events per window with zero prior visualisation. As slack/web surfaces emit, the leaderboard fans out beyond the current kbeads-dominant bar.

panels.title: Residual sentinel writes & authoring gate (M8/M9, ka-0000003187)
M8: residual sentinel writes by resolver source
panels.description: sum by (source)(rate(gardenio_beads_operated_by_writes_by_source_total{kind="sentinel"}[5m])) — of the writes that STILL settle on a sentinel (system:*/fleet:*), which resolver branch produced them. This is the attribution the warn→enforce flip reads: flipping BEADS_AUTHORING_HUMAN_GATE=enforce collapses the fleet_token / legacy branches, so any source with residual here is an unmigrated caller to fix at the source BEFORE flipping. Steady-state target is zero across all sources.

panels.title: M8: empty-resolution writes by resolver source
panels.description: sum by (source)(rate(gardenio_beads_operated_by_writes_by_source_total{kind="empty"}[5m])) — writes whose resolver produced no operator (fail-closed refusal on live-state paths). Under the collapsed ladder (enforce) a header-less fleet/service write lands here instead of binding a sentinel; a sustained rise after the flip is the documented fail-closed amplification signal (bundle ka-0000006634 §5) — correlate with the residual-sentinel panel to see which callers moved sentinel→refused.

panels.title: M9: authoring-gate outcomes by bead_type & action
panels.description: sum by (bead_type, action)(rate(gardenio_beads_authoring_human_gate_total[5m])) — the staged warn→enforce authoring gate on autonomous bead types (trigger/schedule). action=allowed_warn is the residual non-human autonomous authoring a flip to enforce WOULD refuse: drive it to zero (all authoring on action=allowed_human) before flipping BEADS_AUTHORING_HUMAN_GATE=enforce. action=refused counts what enforce blocks post-flip.

defaults.noValue: the gardenio_beads_authoring_human_gate_total counter recorded nothing in the selected range. Series appear per (bead_type, action) once the gate evaluates traffic; a blank panel cannot tell an idle gate from a daemon that stopped exporting — confirm with `up{component="beads"} == 1`.

panels.title: Autonomous authoring warn residual (24h)
panels.description: sum(increase(gardenio_beads_authoring_human_gate_total{action="allowed_warn"}[24h])) — the go/no-go number for the enforce flip: how many autonomous beads in the last 24h were authored with a NON-human operator (would be refused under enforce). Must be 0 for a clean flip. Empty-branch liveness: the `or vector(0)` fallback is gated on `up{component="beads"} == 1`, so a green 0 means the gate really did evaluate writes without warning, not that the daemon stopped exporting.

defaults.noValue: exporter dark — the beads scrape is down, so this reading is unknown rather than 0

panels.title: Reference-extract latency — p50 / p90 / p99

defaults.noValue: no reference-extraction samples in the window — either nothing was extracted, or the counter is not reporting

panels.description: Latency of the typed-mention/reference extractor that runs on every bead write. It sits in the write path, so a rising tail here shows up as slow `kd create` for every agent.

panels.title: Write classification inventory by kind × provider (window)

defaults.noValue: no operated_by write samples in the window — either nothing wrote, or the counter is not reporting

panels.description: Every operated_by write in the range, by kind (real / sentinel / empty) and provider — the sortable inventory behind M2. `real` should dominate; `sentinel` and `empty` are the residual this board exists to drive to zero.

title: Kbeads — operated_by attribution
description: Rollout and health of operated_by attribution in kbeads: header arrival by auth type, write classification (real vs sentinel vs empty), resolver errors and agent-bead fallback, ambiguous-name detections, reference-extraction throughput and the human-authoring gate. Open this to check that bead writes are attributed to a real operator rather than a sentinel.
